svg.aria-label: The six GenEval tasks with prompt counts and pass rules, and the paper's own attribute binding and position examples
svg.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.text: GenEval has six tasks, 553 prompts in all: what a pass needs, and where each one sits in your tables
each of the two named objects is found at least once
the number of boxes for the object matches the asked number (2, 3 or 4)
the object is found and its colour, read by CLIP, matches
both found, and the second is above, below, left or right of the first as asked
both found, and each one's colour matches the colour named for it
Prompt counts sum to 553 (GenEval paper Table 1, page 5). Only the two-object rule was read from the code; the other rules are the task descriptions on pages 4 and 5.
The paper's own examples for two tasks we have no render of ours for
Attribute binding (page 2, Figure 1): "a purple backpack and a white umbrella". The
detector finds an umbrella and a backpack, CLIP reads the umbrellas as purple and yellow,
Position (page 3, Figure 2): "a wine glass right of a hot dog". GenEval passes the left
image and fails the right one ("found above hot dog"); CLIPScore ranks them the other
Both pictures are cropped from the GenEval paper (arXiv 2310.11513) and shown for private study; they are labelled as the paper's, not ours.
